governanceNotes: D1 batch 28 (2026-09-23): one bounded asthma association authored from the shared-eosinophilic-inflammation literature with the distinct-entity literature recorded as a live guard; the asthma target already carries six incoming edges from distinct mechanisms (churg-strauss-syndrome, nasal-polyps, gerd, bronchiolitis, allergic-rhinitis, atopic-dermatitis-eczema), and this edge adds a separate eosinophilic-airway-inflammatory pathway, not a restatement of any existing one.

The asthma target is used rather than the plural or variant identities; no cough-variant-asthma edge is authored because CVA is defined by bronchial hyperresponsiveness that NAEB lacks by definition (identity-mismatch guard, ME-41 pattern).

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Non-asthmatic eosinophilic bronchitis and eosinophilic asthma share the same sputum-eosinophilic airway inflammation and corticosteroid responsiveness while differing in airflow obstruction and bronchial hyperresponsiveness (Lai 2017/2018 review); NAEB patients show elevated airway eosinophil progenitors comparable to eosinophilic asthma (Zhan 2022), and transcriptomic work links FCN1+ macrophage activation to airway remodeling across eosinophilic airway disease (Wu 2024).
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established at the mapping level: the long-term follow-up literature treats NAEB as a distinct entity rather than an early stage of asthma, CT imaging shows maintained airway patency without wall thickening in NAEB (Siddiqui 2009), and no prospective progression-rate evidence demonstrates that EB causes later asthma; the shared inflammation could as easily reflect a common eosinophilic diathesis.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A hypothesized eosinophilic-airway-progression pathway: sustained airway eosinophilic inflammation with elevated eosinophil progenitors releases cationic proteins, leukotrienes, and profibrotic mediators that over time could induce basement-membrane thickening, airway smooth-muscle changes, and bronchial hyperresponsiveness - the phenotype shift that would define asthma; the cited imaging and follow-up evidence shows this transition neither occurs in most patients nor produces the geometric remodeling of asthmatic airways, so the pathway remains an unproven subset hypothesis.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The two conditions share inflammatory biology, but the natural-history evidence on record contests rather than supports progression: no cohort quantifies EB-to-asthma transition rate, airway geometry and clinical follow-up weigh against an early-asthma reading, and a new asthma diagnosis after EB requires documented variable airflow obstruction or bronchial hyperresponsiveness, not eosinophilia alone; no probability estimate is asserted.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Documented NAEB by induced-sputum eosinophilia without bronchial hyperresponsiveness at index; subsequent asthma diagnosis by documented variable airflow obstruction or positive bronchoprovocation with chronology; serial spirometry or FeNO trend; exclusion of antecedent or misdiagnosed asthma at the EB index; smoking and occupational exposure review; pulmonology assessment of the individual relationship
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Cough-variant asthma misdiagnosed as NAEB at the index evaluation
Antecedent asthma in remission rather than new-onset disease
Occupational or irritant-induced airway disease from workplace exposure
GERD or upper-airway cough syndrome driving cough independent of asthma
COPD or chronic bronchitis with fixed obstruction

evidenceGaps: Documented NAEB by induced-sputum eosinophilia without bronchial hyperresponsiveness at index; subsequent asthma diagnosis by documented variable airflow obstruction or positive bronchoprovocation with chronology; serial spirometry or FeNO trend; exclusion of antecedent or misdiagnosed asthma at the EB index; smoking and occupational exposure review; pulmonology assessment of the individual relationship
suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY: the shared eosinophilic biology is well documented, but the distinct-entity follow-up literature and the absence of remodeling on CT cap the claim; progression remains an unproven subset hypothesis and no causation is forced.

sourceReferences.citation: Lai K, Chen R, Peng W, Zhan W. Non-asthmatic eosinophilic bronchitis and its relationship with asthma. Pulm Pharmacol Ther. 2017 Dec;47:66-71. PMID 28687463.
sourceReferences.note: Review of the NAEB-asthma relationship: NAEB shares eosinophilic airway inflammation and corticosteroid responsiveness with asthma but lacks airflow obstruction and bronchial hyperresponsiveness; long-term follow-up supports NAEB as a distinct entity rather than an early stage of asthma, with high relapse after treatment - the shared-biology anchor and the distinct-entity guard.
